title: Agent factory
tagline: A repo-agnostic system where agents write, test and review every pull request, and a human decides only what needs judgment.
why: Of the last 100 merged pull requests in the pipeline repo (first-party count of public PR history, 5 November 2026), 46 came from an external autonomous builder whose trial ended on 6 November, and all 41 reviews were left from one account. The do-nothing baseline is one person relaying and approving every change, which caps throughput at his attention.
mission: A portable gate any repo can adopt. By design, tests run PR code with no credentials, a reviewer agent sees only the diff, as data, with no tools, and each change is sorted into a risk tier. Low-risk tiers will merge without a human; privacy code, migrations and workflow files will always stop for a person.
destination: A reference-only pull request merges with no human touch, a guarded one stops for review, and the reviewer has been back-tested on a labelled set of past pull requests. A day-14 read-out decides whether it stays.
showcase: Trust-boundary design for agents: untrusted text, private data and write access never meet in one job
Failing closed: a missing or malformed verdict, an expired token or a usage limit blocks the merge instead of passing it
Red-teaming a design before building it, and treating its blockers as entry criteria rather than backlog
Risk tiering, where anything the rules don't recognise defaults to the strictest tier
Holding an agent system to a do-nothing baseline and a day-14 kill rule, so quality per token decides whether it stays

milestones.title: Design, systems analysis, eval plan and red-team review
Go decision on separate identities, agent review on every code PR, and the brief contract
Portable core: test workflow with no secrets, gate workflow defined from the base branch
milestones.note: Built in its own public repository and through three independent review rounds. It has run only in local tests so far.

milestones.title: Separate identities for authoring, approving and merging
Pilot on this pipeline repo: one trial PR per risk tier, with auto-merge off

decisions.decision: Split identities: an agent account authors, an app approves low-risk tiers, and a person approves guarded paths in the browser.
decisions.why: Authoring, approving and merging should be distinct roles that can be audited separately.

decisions.decision: Run agent code review on every code PR, with no rubric or score, and a kill rule at day 14.
decisions.why: A reviewer that runs on every change has to prove it's worth its cost, so the test is quality per token.

decisions.decision: Keep the gate's core in its own public repository, so each project adopts it by pinning a version.
decisions.why: A repo-agnostic system needs one home and one version history, not a copy per project.

decisions.decision: Research briefs become a reading rather than an approval; drafts arrive with a pre-review, and nothing publishes without Alex.
decisions.why: Human time goes to judgment calls, not to thumbs-ups on work an agent can check.

open.question: After the pilot, back-test a reviewer from a second model provider against the in-house reviewer, and keep it only if it catches real defects the first one misses?

risks.risk: Prompt injection: a diff can carry text written to talk the reviewer into approving.
risks.mitigation: By design, the reviewer will get a stripped diff only, no tools and no PR text, and will need a positive verdict to pass.

risks.risk: The gate has run only in local tests; its behaviour on GitHub, such as approvals and re-runs after a human review, is unproven.
risks.mitigation: One trial PR per risk tier with auto-merge off, before anything merges on its own.

risks.risk: A reviewer on every PR can spend tokens without catching defects.
risks.mitigation: The day-14 read-out compares cost and catches with the baseline, and the kill rule removes it if it doesn't pay.

log.text: Portable core opened for review in its own public repository. Three independent review rounds closed their findings.
Go decision taken on all three design questions. Phase 0 build started.
The design went through independent analyses and a red-team pass. Its blockers became entry criteria for the build.
